cases.answer: In the elderly diabetic HFpEF cohort, after six months of SGLT2i treatment, oxidative-stress biomarkers improved significantly. Nox-2 fell from 1.24 ± 0.71 to 1.01 ± 0.04 nmol/L (p < 0.0001). 8-Isoprostane fell from 70.41 ± 5.67 to 65.67 ± 4.16 pg/mL (p < 0.0001). Platelet-activation markers also improved. Sp-Selectin fell from 125.92 ± 12.84 to 101.84 ± 4.42 ng/mL (p < 0.0001). Gp-VI fell from 60.99 ± 6.36 to 49.51 ± 5.89 (p < 0.0001).

cases.answer: The trial predefined non-inferiority as the upper bound of the 95% CI for the HbA1c treatment difference being < 0.4% (margin 0.4). The adjusted (ANCOVA, least-square mean) result was a change of −2.22% with generic semaglutide versus −2.17% with innovator. The LSM difference was −0.05% (95% CI −0.19 to 0.09). The upper bound of 0.09 was well below the 0.4% margin, so non-inferiority was met.

cases.answer: In He et al., the all-eight-trial sensitivity analysis used post-treatment final values, which are more susceptible to baseline imbalance than change-score analyses. Five of the eight trials did not clearly report random sequence generation, none used blinding or placebo control, and heterogeneity was extreme (I² = 91–99%). The authors therefore treated it as supportive only and cautiously interpreted, and said it was not sufficient to override the more conservative change-score primary analysis, despite statistical significance (HbA1c MD −1.21, 95% CI −1.99 to −0.43).

At 6 months the difference was −0.6% (95% CI −1.4% to 0.2%; −6.9 mmol/mol; P=.12), lower but not statistically significant. A sensitivity analysis excluding participants who never participated was significant at both time points (−1%, P=.01 at 3 months; −0.8%, P=.046 at 6 months).
